scoring.formula: ambiguity% = points / applicable_checkpoints * 100 ; marks: OK=0, WARN=0.5, FAIL=1
scoring.naRationale: Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) is scored N/A on every unit: the budget/timeline/team/compliance/performance axes are owned by meta/constraints.md, which is outside this domain's scope. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is scored N/A on the four mechanism sub-domains (04.01, 04.03, 04.04, 04.05); it is scored on the domain root and on 04.02, both of which name >=3 incumbents with a specific capability gap and a defensible moat.

findings.claim: opportunities-casting-cx.md contradicts itself on the alert cap within one cross-cut: CX-01 states both that a post may alert a subscriber exactly once ever and that the cap is two per user per post.
findings.evidence: opportunities-casting-cx.md:45-46 - "compensation **edits must never re-fire** the alert ... and publication `bump` must not re-fire either - **one alert per post per subscriber, ever**." ; opportunities-casting-cx.md:66 - "4. **Notification fan-out**: Publication is the fan-out's sole trigger; bump and edit are excluded by rule (D-13). Targeting-widening is the only legal cause of a second alert (**cap 2 lifetime per user/post**)." ; opportunities-casting-cx.md:19 (CX-01 map row) - "Publication gate is the fan-out's **sole** trigger". The canonical decision is 04.02.04 D-12 (line 244): "**Two alerts per (user, post), lifetime.** The second is spent on an eligibility-widening edit or a deadline escalation - whichever comes first", and 04.02.04:149 makes a deadline escalation an alert with no publication event behind it: "Post's deadline burns from > 14d into 72h | Tier escalates Digest -> Timely (D-06). Consumes alert 2 of 2."
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the fan-out from the domain CX file reads line 46 and enforces a one-alert-ever idempotency key on (user, post). A deadline escalation on an open call then never fires, so the 'Closes in 2 days' alert that 04.02.04 D-06 exists to deliver is silently dropped for every subscriber who was alerted at publication - i.e. all of them. Reading line 66 instead yields a cap of 2 and a working escalation. Both readings are supported by the same cross-cut, 20 lines apart, with no marker on either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the fan-out cap is 1 or 2 per (user, post), and whether any event other than publication may fire an alert at all.
findings.fix: Delete the absolute claim at line 46 and the word 'sole' at line 19; restate CX-01 as: publication is the fan-out's only *first-alert* trigger; bump and compensation edits never re-fire; targeting-widening and deadline escalation each may consume the second and last alert, cap 2 lifetime per (user, post) per 04.02.04 D-12.

findings.claim: 04.07 specifies 'waitlisted' as a third disposition tier that goes out to applicants, while its own resolved Q-02 and the closed disposition vocabulary in 04.05.01 both forbid telling an applicant a waitlist state at all.
findings.evidence: 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md:35 - "| Outcome | Won / not selected | **Tiered** - accepted, waitlisted, rejected |" ; :45 - "5. Tiered dispositions go out - accepted, waitlisted, rejected. All of them (04.05.01)." ; :67 - "| Waitlisted | Tier assigned | See Q-02 - the rot state |" ; contradicted by its own :102 - "Q-02 ... RESOLVED - ... a waitlisted act is either a *backup* - which is a shortlist rank (CX-02), not a hold - or a hold carrying a named blocker and a dated resolve-by; and 04.04.01 D-06 tells the applicant **a date, not a state**." ; and by 04.04.01 D-06 (line 212) - "The applicant is told **a date, not a state** - 'You'll hear by 14 Aug' ... Never 'you're a maybe' (raises hope, leaks a rank ...)" ; and by 04.05.01's disposition table (lines 54-62), whose seven values contain no 'waitlisted'.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer reading 04.07's Behavior table, Happy Path and States builds a third disposition value 'waitlisted', sends it to (say) 200 of 2000 acts, and closes their pipeline entries with it. An implementer reading Q-02 builds no such value: backups become shortlist ranks that are never disclosed, holds carry a blocker plus a resolve-by, and every applicant is told only a date. The two products tell 200 acts materially different things, and only one of them is consistent with 04.05.01's obligation arithmetic (a 'waitlisted' notice is not in the value table, so it discharges nothing and the debt stays open).
findings.forcedInvention: Whether 'waitlisted' is a disposition value, a shortlist rank, or a hold; and what the waitlisted act is actually told.
findings.fix: Rewrite 04.07's Outcome row, Happy Path step 5 and the Waitlisted state to match Q-02's resolution: two disposition tiers (accepted / not selected) plus an internal backup rank or blocker-carrying hold that renders to the applicant as a date only.

findings.claim: The member-wanted lifecycle has three mutually incompatible lifespans across two files: unbounded, a 60-day submission cutoff, and a 90-day board exit.
findings.evidence: 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:36 - "| Lifecycle | Deadline-bound | **Open-ended; runs for months** |" ; :63 - "| Open | Ad posted | Live, open-ended, **no deadline** |" ; contradicted by 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:62-66 (D-06) - "any post with no poster activity for a type-scoped interval - ... **30 days for member-wanted** ... renders a 'Poster hasn't touched this since {date}' marker and sinks below fresh posts of equal fit. **At 2x the interval it auto-tombstones** as 'Assumed stale - no response from the poster' and **stops accepting submissions**." ; and by 04.02.01:60 - "| Member wanted (04.06) | Recency, 90-day half-life | Poster closes it, **or 90 days elapse** | 14 days |" ; and 04.02.01:218 - "the longest-half-life listing on the board (**90 days**)".
findings.failureScenario: A band posts 'bassist wanted' and does not touch it for 61 days, which 04.06 says is normal ('runs for months'). Under 04.02.01 D-06 the ad auto-tombstones at day 60 and stops accepting submissions; under D-05's own table it is still on the board until day 90; under 04.06 it never expires at all. A hobbyist who answers on day 75 either submits successfully, is refused, or cannot see the ad, depending on which rule the implementer encoded. The three statements also cannot be reconciled arithmetically inside 04.02.01 alone: auto-tombstone at 2x30=60 days plus a 14-day tombstone window removes the listing at day 74, not day 90.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a member-wanted ad expires; if so at 60 or 90 days; and whether expiry stops submissions or only de-ranks the listing.
findings.fix: Pick one lifespan and state it in both files. If member-wanted is genuinely open-ended, exempt it from D-06's auto-tombstone and delete the 90-day board-exit condition; if it is bounded, correct 04.06's Lifecycle row and Open state and reconcile the 60-day and 90-day numbers.

findings.claim: 04.01.01's flagship happy path inherits compensation from the source booking and relies on that to clear the gate without interaction; 04.01.03 D-17 forbids exactly that, every time, with no exception.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:104 - "2. System opens the composer **pre-filled from the show**: date (venue-local, D-10), venue, **compensation (inherited from the booking)**, setlist (from 18), and the hirer" ; :108-111 - "4. Poster taps publish. The compensation gate evaluates synchronously (CX-01), and **passes without interaction because the fee came from the booking.** ... **Three interactions from 'drummer dropped out' to 'asking Sam'.**" ; :27 - "raised from a booked show (D-02) a dep call is **type -> slot -> confirm, three interactions**, because the show already knows the date, venue, **fee** and setlist" ; D-02 at :263 - "The platform already holds the show, the setlist, the project and **the fee**." ; flatly contradicted by 04.01.03-compensation-spec-work-guardrails.md D-17 at :223 - "**Compensation is never pre-filled from the source booking**, even when the post is raised from context (04.01.01 D-02) | Inheriting the fee leaks the fixer's margin to the dep (DT-15)." ; and its edge case :140 - "| Poster raises a dep call from their own booked show (04.01.01 D-02) | Date, venue and setlist inherit. **Compensation does not** (DT-15) ... | **Compensation step is blank and required, every time** |" ; and Happy Path step 1 at :87 - "Compensation is **never pre-filled from the source booking** even when the post was raised from context". The claim is repeated downstream at 04.02.03:40 and 04.04.04:38 ("date, venue, setlist and fee already known").
findings.failureScenario: Two implementers build the dep-out composer. One follows 04.01.01 and pre-fills the fee from Show #123, so the gate passes silently and the flow is three taps - and the dep is shown the bandleader's own booking fee, which is precisely the fixer's-margin leak 04.01.03 DT-15 identifies as a concrete privacy failure. The other follows D-17, leaves the field blank and required, and the flagship 'three interactions' claim is false (the poster must declare six compensation facets before publishing). This is not a wording slip: it is two Decisions of record (04.01.01 D-02 and 04.01.03 D-17) asserting opposite behaviour on the same field, and 04.01.01's Cross-Cut Notes to 04.01.03 (:237) list what that file changed for them without mentioning D-17 at all.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the composer pre-fills compensation from the source booking, and consequently whether the domain's headline dep-out flow is three interactions or three-plus-a-full-compensation-declaration.
findings.fix: Amend 04.01.01: strike 'compensation (inherited from the booking)' from Happy Path A step 2, strike 'passes without interaction because the fee came from the booking' from step 4, remove 'fee' from D-02's and the Role Lens's inherited-facts list, and restate the interaction count. Add D-17 to 04.01.01's Cross-Cut Notes for 04.01.03. Correct the same claim at 04.02.03:40 and 04.04.04:38.

findings.claim: The 25-slot limit is a soft ceiling in the Behavior section, the Decisions table and the domain CX, and a hard refusal in the Edge Cases table.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:45-46 - "**Soft ceiling: 25 slots per post** - past that it is a hiring round, and the shape that serves it is the open call (04.07)" ; D-08 at :269 - "**The slot is the fillable unit; the post is the container.** Lifecycle is per slot; the post's status follows its slots. **Soft ceiling 25 slots**" ; opportunities-casting-cx.md:29 (CX-11) - "the 25-slot **soft** ceiling routes here" ; contradicted by 04.01.01:148 - "| Post needs 30 slots (a festival's whole crew) | **Refused above 25**; routed to the open call shape (04.07), which has the batch review a 30-slot spine post would need and doesn't have | \"That's a hiring round, not an opportunity - open calls handle 30 slots properly.\" |"
findings.failureScenario: A festival tries to post one call for 30 crew slots. Under D-08's 'soft ceiling' the composer warns and publishes; under the edge case it refuses and redirects to 04.07 - which is a different type with a different date semantics, a batch-locked queue and tiered outcomes, so the redirect is not cosmetic. Whether the 30-slot post exists at all differs between implementations, and the Decisions table (normally authoritative) and the Edge Cases table (normally concrete) point opposite ways.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether 25 slots is enforced or advisory.
findings.fix: Choose one word. If refusal is intended, change 'Soft ceiling' to 'Hard ceiling' at 04.01.01:45 and in D-08, and drop 'soft' from domain CX-11. If a warning is intended, rewrite the 30-slot edge case as warn-and-suggest.

findings.claim: 04.01.02's edge-case table states the invite-vs-eligibility conflict is unresolved and shows a confirmation prompt, while its own Open Questions table records it as resolved with an inform-after-the-fact behaviour.
findings.evidence: 04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:47 - "| Invited person fails eligibility criteria (CX-03) | **Unresolved and important.** Recommendation carried to Step 5: honour the invite, show the poster the mismatch ... | Poster: \"Sam doesn't meet 'reads notation' - **invite anyway?**\" |" ; contradicted by its own Q-01 at :100 - "~~Invite vs eligibility conflict (CX-03) - does an explicit invite waive a failed criterion?~~ ✅ **RESOLVED - yes.** An **explicit invite waives eligibility**; the mismatch is shown to the poster on the invite and on the submission, never silently suppressed" ; and by 04.01.04 D-05 at :102 and its edge case at :58 - "Invite **waives** eligibility (D-05) ... | Applicant: no block, normal submit. Poster: \"You invited them, but they don't read charts - **invited anyway.**\" |" (a past-tense statement, not a question). The same stale 'unresolved' framing survives at 04.01-opportunity-posting-targeting-cx.md:84-86 ("The system must decide whether targeting overrides eligibility ... or eligibility overrides targeting") and :101-103 ("**This is the crux** ... **Recommendation** to carry into Step 5"), and at opportunities-casting-cx.md:93 ("An invited-but-ineligible person is the unresolved intersection (04.01 CX-03)").
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the invite composer from the edge-case table adds a blocking confirmation dialogue ('invite anyway?') before the invite is sent - which on the dep circuit is exactly the confirmation step 04.01.02 D-03 rejects for time-pressured flows ('under dep-call time pressure a confirmation dialogue is an unanswered notification, and the gig goes unfilled'). An implementer following D-05 sends the invite immediately and surfaces the mismatch as information. Different number of taps, different failure mode under a 9pm clock.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the eligibility mismatch on an invited candidate is a pre-send confirmation gate or a post-send disclosure.
findings.fix: Rewrite 04.01.02's edge-case row to cite D-05 as resolved and change its copy to the declarative form used in 04.01.04:58. Update 04.01's CX-03 synthesis and the domain CX-02 line that still calls the intersection unresolved.

findings.claim: The trigger for the 'filled elsewhere' prompt - the mechanism the domain's stated beachhead depends on - is a threshold with no value for any of the twelve types, and no tracked question asks for one.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:166 - "`Filled elsewhere` is a **first-class, one-tap terminal action** offered proactively **on any post older than its type's typical fill window**." No 'typical fill window' value appears anywhere in the domain for any type; the taxonomy table (:76-89) carries columns for origin, date semantics, unpaid legitimacy and casting class, and no fill window. Contrast the same file's D-13 at :274, which does state its intervals and says so: "Bump: 1 per rolling 24h, max 3 per post ... **Intervals stated as the senior-dev call; tunable at `/create-prd`.**" The dependency is load-bearing per :243 - "Three triggers originate here: expiry, withdrawal, and **`filled elsewhere`** (DT-07). The last is the one that matters ... the domain's beachhead (D-04) is undeliverable without it." Q-01..Q-08 of 04.01.01 cover none of it.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A sets the window to 24 hours for every type, so a festival open call running 18 months out (permitted explicitly at :179 - 'No upper bound') is asked 'Did you fill this?' the day after it opens, 17 months early, training the poster to dismiss the prompt. Implementer B sets it to two weeks, so a 9pm dep call for tomorrow night is never prompted at all and rots with 12 applicants - the precise failure DT-07 and domain D-04 exist to prevent. Both are consistent with the text.
findings.forcedInvention: A fill-window value for each of the twelve taxonomy types.
findings.fix: Add a fill-window column to the taxonomy table with a stated senior-dev default per type, marked tunable at /create-prd in the same form D-13 already uses, or open an owned question for it.

findings.claim: The blocked-invitee case is marked pending against a stage that has run and closed, has no owner, and is covered by none of the file's three open questions - so a cascade behaviour is genuinely undefined and untracked.
findings.evidence: 04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:49 - "| Poster targets someone who has blocked them | Invite silently fails - but silently to *whom*? Telling the poster leaks the block. | `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` - a Trust & Safety (24) boundary. |" The stage is dead per the same file's Q-02 at :101 ("Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, **which has run and left this open**"). The file's Open Questions are Q-01 (invite vs eligibility, resolved), Q-02 (confidentiality as a separate property) and Q-03 (trusted-network cold start) - none covers the blocked invitee. The adjacent row at :54 does define an analogous rule for a different cause ("Invited person deletes their account / is suspended before the cascade reaches them | Treated as unavailable at that position: cascade advances to the next name rather than stalling. No leak of *why* they dropped"), but it is scoped to deletion and suspension.
findings.failureScenario: A bandleader's ranked dep list contains someone who has blocked them. Implementer A applies the neighbouring rule and silently advances the cascade, so the poster sees 'Skipping to your next choice' with no reason. Implementer B surfaces a delivery failure to the poster, which discloses the block and hands a harasser a confirmation signal - the exact leak 04.01.01 D-14 and 04.02.01:159 are built to prevent elsewhere. Nothing in the tree adjudicates it and no owner is on the hook.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a blocked target is skipped silently, and what (if anything) the poster is told.
findings.fix: Either extend the row at :54 to cover blocks explicitly (skip silently, no reason disclosed, cascade advances) or add an owned Q-04 pointed at /create-prd-security alongside the 24 boundary.

findings.claim: 04.01.01 D-13 and its Cross-Cut Notes assert an absolute one-alert-per-subscriber-per-post rule and that publication is the fan-out's sole trigger; 04.02.04 D-12, which owns the alert pipe, sets the cap at two and names two non-publication triggers.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:128 - "6. On pass, the post enters `published` and is released to the board (04.02.01) and the alert fan-out (04.02.04). **The fan-out fires once per post per subscriber, ever (D-13).**" ; :240 - "Touches **04.02.04 Alert Subscriptions & Delivery** ... Publication is the fan-out's **sole** trigger, and **bump must not re-fire it** (D-13) - **one alert per post per subscriber, ever.**" ; :198 - "| Published | Gate passed; >=1 slot open | Live on board, **alerts fanned out once** (D-13), submission open |" ; contradicted by 04.02.04-alert-subscriptions-delivery.md D-12 at :244 - "**Two alerts per (user, post), lifetime.** The second is spent on an eligibility-widening edit or a deadline escalation - whichever comes first" ; :86 - "| Alerts per (user, post) | **2 lifetime** (D-12) | The first is the match. The second is spent on whichever comes first: an eligibility-widening edit (04.01.02) or a deadline escalation (D-06). A third would be an edit-loop spam vector. |" ; :148 - "| Post edited to widen targeting (invite-only -> network) | The recipient is **newly eligible** - this is the one legal re-alert. **Consumes alert 2 of 2** (D-12). |" ; :149 - "| Post's deadline burns from > 14d into 72h | Tier escalates Digest -> Timely (D-06). **Consumes alert 2 of 2.** |"
findings.failureScenario: The fan-out is built from 04.01.01 (the file that owns the post and its publication event) with a hard one-per-(user,post) idempotency key. Targeting escalation then cannot alert the newly-entitled network tier - so 04.01.02 D-03's whole escalation ladder ('the post escalates one rung out, and the poster is told') reaches nobody by push - and deadline escalation cannot fire, so 04.02.04 D-06's clock-promotes-tier mechanism is dead for anyone already alerted. Read from 04.02.04 instead, both work. The two files disagree on a hard integer.
findings.forcedInvention: The alert cap per (user, post) and the legal set of alert triggers.
findings.fix: Correct 04.01.01:128, :198 and :240 to 'at most one alert per subscriber at publication; a second is permitted only for targeting-widening or deadline escalation, cap 2 lifetime (04.02.04 D-12)', and drop the word 'sole'.

findings.claim: Three of this unit's CX synthesis slots are left as bare pending markers pointed at a stage that has run and closed, with no owner - and one of them has no answer anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: 04.02-discovery-matching-alerts-cx.md:102-104 (CX-03 q5) - "A gig cancelling should arguably *un*-suppress alerts already swallowed - replaying missed alerts on a freed evening is a genuinely novel behaviour and nobody asked for it. `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`" ; :143 (CX-05 q3) - "3. **Permission intersection**: `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`" ; :146 (CX-05 q5) - "5. **State transition conflict**: `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`". CX-05 q5 - the state-transition conflict between a moving material score and an already-granted quiet-hours override - has no answer anywhere.
findings.failureScenario: The one genuinely open slot bites where it is most expensive: material confidence is the only input that reaches Critical (04.02.04 D-05) and Critical overrides quiet hours (D-08). If the setlist changes after a Critical was computed but before delivery, nothing states whether the override is revoked, so an implementer either wakes a musician at 11pm on a confidence score that is no longer true, or silently downgrades a genuine emergency alert. 04.02.04:212 already flags the compounding risk in the same breath ('an overstated confidence here does not just mis-rank, it **buys a quiet-hours override it did not earn**') without closing it.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Critical tier already computed survives a material-score invalidation, and what the recipient gets if it does not.
findings.fix: Fold 04.02.04 D-11 and D-14 into CX-03 q5 and CX-05 q3 as answers, and give CX-05 q5 an owned question against /create-prd-architecture (it is the same input-freshness family as 04.02.03's Stale state, F14).

findings.claim: 04.02.03 declares a Stale state whose entire user-visible behaviour is a pending marker aimed at a closed stage, with no owner and no covering open question - and the undefined behaviour changes who is offered the gig.
findings.evidence: 04.02.03-material-aware-dep-matching.md:64 - "| Stale | Setlist changed post-scoring | `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |" ; :52 - "| Setlist changes after matching | Score invalidated. Setlists change constantly, often on the day. | `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` - **re-score, or accept staleness?** |" The stage is closed per the same file's Q-03 at :99 ("Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5"). Implementer B accepts staleness and asks the person who knew the old set. Under 04.04.04 the first yes ends the slot, so the two implementations put different humans on stage - and neither behaviour is stated, including what the poster is shown while the pool is stale.

findings.claim: The candidacy is keyed on role in 04.03.01 and on slot in 04.01.01 and 04.05.01; because one post can carry two slots with the same role, the keys are not interchangeable and the disposition arithmetic differs.
findings.evidence: 04.03.01-structured-submission.md D-05 at :195 - "A submission is identified by **(submitting entity, post, role)** ... Two roles means two candidacies and two dispositions owed. **Whether a post can carry multiple roles is 04.01.01's to answer (Q-05).**" ; its Q-05 at :214 - "**Can one post carry more than one role/chair?** (D-05, DT-05.) ... **This is 04.01.01's decision, not this feature's.**" ; but 04.01.01 already decided it, and decided on the slot rather than the role - D-08 at :269 - "**The slot is the fillable unit; the post is the container.** Lifecycle is per slot" ; :38-40 - "Each **slot** carries a role, a count, its own eligibility criteria and its own compensation value" ; :29 - Operator posts are "the only ones routinely **multi-slot** (2 riggers + 1 LD for one load-in - D-08)" - i.e. two slots sharing the role 'rigger' ; and 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md D-07 at :241 - "**The obligation is per submission, per slot.** Post state is **derived**, never set" ; :42 - "| **Granularity** | Per submission, per **slot** ... |" ; :154 - "| **Multi-slot post: 3 slots filled, 1 still live** | Obligation is per slot (D-07) |"
findings.failureScenario: An Operator posts one crew call with three slots: rigger x1, rigger x1 (different call times), LD x1. A candidate applies to both rigger slots. Under 04.03.01 D-05 the key (entity, post, role) collapses them into one candidacy and the second application supersedes the first (D-02: 'Resubmission supersedes rather than duplicates'), silently deleting a real candidacy - exactly the defect DT-05 says D-05 was introduced to fix. Under 04.01.01 D-08 and 04.05.01 D-07 they are two candidacies with two independent debts and two dispositions. The same divergence propagates into per-slot eligibility criteria and per-slot compensation (04.01.01:39), which a role-keyed submission cannot address, and into domain CX-08's stated arithmetic ('two candidacies = two dispositions owed').
findings.forcedInvention: The submission's foreign key - slot or role - and therefore how many candidacies, how many dispositions and which eligibility set apply.
findings.fix: Re-key the submission on (submitting entity, slot) per 04.01.01 D-08, retire 04.03.01 Q-05 as already answered by D-08, and update D-05, DT-05, domain CX-08 and 04.05.01's 'two roles' phrasing to speak of slots.

findings.claim: The type-scoped free-text question ceiling names a type that does not exist in the closed taxonomy and leaves five of the twelve real types without a ceiling.
findings.evidence: 04.03.01-structured-submission.md D-08 at :198 - "Type-scoped ceiling - **0 for dep-call/urgent types, 1 for session call / crew / member-wanted, 3 for brief / A&R / audition / open call**, hard platform ceiling 3." The taxonomy is closed and platform-curated per 04.01.01 D-04 (:265) and enumerates twelve types (:78-89): dep/sub call, session call, function/private hire, audition/casting call, brief/RFP, crew/technical labour, festival/showcase/competition open call, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, member wanted, open-mic/showcase slot, General call. 'A&R' is not among them. Unassigned: function/private hire, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, open-mic/showcase slot, General call.
findings.failureScenario: A wedding-band fixer posts a function gig. The ceiling for that type is unstated, so implementer A allows the platform maximum of 3 questions and implementer B allows 0. Under D-08's own reasoning that choice decides whether triage stays a 40-second job for the highest-volume commercial type in the domain. Separately, a rule keyed on a type name that the closed taxonomy does not contain cannot be evaluated at all.
findings.forcedInvention: A question ceiling for five of the twelve types, and what 'A&R' maps to.
findings.fix: Extend D-08's ceiling list to all twelve taxonomy types and replace 'A&R' with the real type name (brief/RFP, per 04.01.01's table where A&R briefs were folded in).

findings.claim: Blind mode is declared type-scoped but the per-type property table that governs every other type-scoped rule carries no blind-mode column, and only one of twelve types is assigned a value.
findings.evidence: 04.03.04-blind-review-mode.md D-02 at :91 - "Blind mode is **type-scoped** | Incoherent for dep calls (the point is who you are and whether you know the set); coherent for auditions and house/orchestral work." ; its edge case :55 - "| Poster enables blind mode on a dep call | Incoherent ... **Should not be offerable for that type.** | Type-scoped availability |" ; the governing table is 04.01.01:76-89, whose columns are Origin, Date semantics (D-10), Unpaid legit? (D-11), Casting class (D-15) and 'What makes it distinct' - there is no blind-mode column, and only the Audition row mentions it: ":81 - Adds an audition task (04.03.03); **may enable blind mode (04.03.04)**". 04.07 asserts a second coherent case in passing at :43 ("Batch review begins - blind if enabled (04.03.04), **which is coherent here**") without it appearing in the taxonomy.

Where it is offered, 04.04.01 DT-06's cost applies unannounced - blind mode 'removes the engine' of triage, so the close-out obligation stops being cheap for that post, which is the guarantee domain D-04's beachhead rests on.

findings.claim: Five of this unit's CX synthesis slots are blank pending markers aimed at a closed stage with no owner, including three of the five slots on the cross-cut that a sibling's resolved question cites as its own authority.
findings.evidence: 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:103 (CX-03 q3), :105 (CX-03 q5), :154 (CX-05 q3), :155 (CX-05 q4), :156 (CX-05 q5) - each reads only "`[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`". So nobody has stated whether a waived audition notifies anyone, whether a candidate whose evidence later changes loses the waiver, or who may see that a waiver was granted - and there is no owner to ask.

findings.claim: The evidence threshold that waives an audition has no scale, unit or vocabulary - the evidence model it would be expressed over is an unquantified five-row ordinal list.
findings.evidence: 04.03.03-audition-tasks-media-submission.md D-03 at :102 - "**Strong evidence** should **waive** the audition (CX-05)" ; Q-03 resolved at :111 - "a **poster-set threshold** ... *\"Evidence resolved -> threshold met -> audition waived or reduced. Poster-set thresholds, since the judgement is theirs.\"*" ; the quantity the threshold ranges over is 04.03.02's table at :40-46, which is purely ordinal and unnumbered - "Evidence types, in descending order of strength: Verified credit with attestor | Material history | Prior collaboration with the poster's network | Completed engagement history | Self-claimed skills" - with no counts, no recency and no scoring. A comparable rule elsewhere in the domain does state its numbers (04.02.04:52 - Critical requires "material confidence >= 'played this exact set' or 'played >=60% of these songs in the last 24 months'"), but that vocabulary exists only for dep-call material and only inside the alert tiering.
findings.failureScenario: A producer setting up a session call is asked to set a waiver threshold. Implementer A exposes 'at least N attested credits'; implementer B exposes 'material confidence >= 60%' (meaningless for a session, which has a rough rather than a setlist); implementer C exposes a free-text judgement, which defeats the stated purpose of expressing it once as a threshold rather than re-taking it per candidate. The applicant-facing consequence is concrete and stated in D-02: the applicant must be able to see whether a waiver applies **before** spending the time, and they cannot be shown a threshold nobody can express.
findings.forcedInvention: The quantity, scale and per-type vocabulary a waiver threshold is set over.
findings.fix: Define the waiver threshold's domain in 04.03.02 (e.g. count of attested citations matched to the post's requirements, plus recency) and state which types can express it, following the shape 04.02.04:52 already uses for material confidence.

findings.claim: One edge-case row states the deadline is displayed viewer-timezone-first, its own copy renders poster-timezone-first, and 04.02.01 D-12 fixes the opposite primacy for the same fact.
findings.evidence: 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:87 - "| **Deadline stated as \"midnight\"** | **Deadlines are absolute instants displayed in the viewer's local timezone with the poster's timezone named.** ... | \"Closes 00:00 21 Aug BST (that's 19:00 20 Aug your time).\" |" - the copy leads with the poster's zone and parenthesises the viewer's, which is the inverse of the prose ; contradicted by 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md D-12 at :246 - "Dates render in the **opportunity's local timezone**, with the viewer's offset shown when they differ | A gig is at a place. Musicians tour. \"Friday\" means the venue's Friday, and getting this wrong misses gigs." ; and by :90 - "| Date / date range | Rendered in the **opportunity's local timezone** with the viewer's offset shown when they differ (D-12) |"
findings.failureScenario: The board renders '21 Aug' in the venue's zone and the submission screen renders '20 Aug' in the applicant's zone for the same deadline. An applicant in Los Angeles reading a London open call sees two different closing dates on two screens of one flow and misses the window - the failure mode D-12's own rationale names ('getting this wrong misses gigs'). The row also cannot be implemented as written, since its prose and its copy disagree with each other.
findings.forcedInvention: Which timezone leads on a deadline and which is parenthesised.
findings.fix: Align 04.03.01:87's prose with its own copy and with 04.02.01 D-12: the opportunity's zone leads, the viewer's offset is shown when it differs.

findings.claim: Five decisions and two states across two sub-domains are built on a post field - the decide-by date - that the file owning the post object never defines, and no open question anywhere asks for it.
findings.evidence: 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md D-05 at :211 - "every hold has a **resolve-by date bounded by the post's decide-by** (04.01.01)" ; D-06 at :212 - "The applicant is told **a date, not a state** - \"You'll hear by 14 Aug\" | **Derived from the post's decide-by (04.01.01)**" ; :96 - "**Holds carry a blocker and a resolve-by date** defaulting to - and never exceeding - the post's decide-by date (04.01.01)" ; the Dormant state at :158 - "| Dormant | >=1 candidate, 0 triage actions, **>=50% of the publish->decide-by window elapsed** |" ; the Abandoned state at :160 - "| Abandoned | Poster stopped returning; **decide-by reached** with cards untouched |" ; and the file names the risk itself at :192 - "The post's **decide-by date** is the ceiling on every hold's resolve-by (D-05) and the denominator of the `dormant` trigger. **Without a decide-by, D-05's forcing function has no bound.**" 04.05.01 depends on it four more times, including a proposed default computed from it (:254 - "Proposed default if yes: **decide-by + 7 days**"). 04.01.01, which owns the post, never mentions decide-by: its context fields are ":38 - type, acting identity, hirer, decider, date, location, compensation policy", its terms set is D-09's ":270 - type, acting identity, date, location, slot count, compensation, required criteria", and its only expiry rule keys on the event date (":169 - Post's date passes while still `published`"). Contrast 04.05.03 Q-07 (:260), which does track a comparable missing field and says why: "*Status check: `04.01.01` still carries neither field ... so the gap is live.* ... Leaving it unrecorded means the handoff is unbuildable as specified." No equivalent question exists for decide-by.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the queue and finds no decide-by on the post. Option A: treat the event date as the decide-by - which breaks immediately for the types whose date is a delivery deadline (04.01.01 D-10) and for member-wanted, which 04.06:63 says has no deadline at all, so holds get no ceiling, D-06 can promise no date, and the dormant trigger has no denominator. Option B: invent a required decide-by field on every post, changing the composer for all twelve types and adding a mandatory field to the domain's headline three-interaction dep flow. Either way the resolution of 04.04.01's self-described 'most important open question' (Q-01, resolved by D-05) is unbuildable as specified, along with the cheapest anti-ghosting act in the product (D-06).
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Opportunity carries a decide-by date, whether it is mandatory, its default per type, and its relationship to the event date and to types with no deadline.
findings.fix: Add decide-by to 04.01.01's post object as a first-class field with a per-type default and a rule for deadline-less types, and fold it into D-09's terms set (a decide-by change is material). Alternatively open an owned question in the shape of 04.05.03 Q-07 - but the field is referenced as existing by seven downstream statements, so silence is the one option that cannot stand.

findings.claim: The offer fuse is poster-chosen in 04.04.03 and platform-set in 04.04.04, has no length, floor or ceiling for the ordinary non-cascade offer, and its bounding question is closed in a way that covers only cascades.
findings.evidence: 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md D-02 at :246 - "| D-02 | Offers **expire** | Silence stalls the whole chain" - no duration, default or bound anywhere ; D-07 at :251 - "**The offer is irrevocable for its fuse.** The poster cannot change their mind **inside a window they chose**" ; :150 - "| Poster withdraws a live offer because they changed their mind | **No such button** (D-07) ... A poster who wants the option to change their mind has one available: **a shorter fuse.** |" ; :170 - "the *length* of that window is **04.04.04 Q-03**, and this file contributes the constraint that bounds it: **a poster-set fuse with no ceiling** lets a poster impose an unbounded free option on the candidate" ; but 04.04.04-urgent-fill-first-accept-cascade.md D-05 at :97 decides the opposite and only for cascades - "**Fuse is platform-set by urgency tier with a ~3-minute floor; the poster can escalate urgency but not shorten below the floor** | A free poster-set fuse strands the whole list (DT-04)." ; and its Q-03 at :105 is closed - "~~Fuse length - poster-set, or platform-set by urgency?~~ **Resolved (DT-04, D-05): platform-set by urgency tier, ~3-min floor, poster may escalate not shorten.** What remains open is only the exact tier-to-minutes table."
findings.failureScenario: A venue offers a support slot from a shortlist. There is no cascade, so 04.04.04 D-05 does not apply on its face; 04.04.03 D-07 says the poster chose the window and offers 'a shorter fuse' as their only legitimate route to optionality, so implementer A ships a poster-set duration field with no ceiling - and a 14-day fuse blocks the act's date for a fortnight while committing the venue to nothing, the exact asymmetry DT-06 identifies and claims to have bounded. Implementer B reads 04.04.04 D-05 as global, so the field does not exist and the poster cannot shorten anything, which removes D-07's stated mitigation entirely. Neither implementer has a default duration to fall back on, and the question that was supposed to supply the bound is marked resolved for a different path.
findings.forcedInvention: Who sets the non-cascade offer fuse, its default length, and whether a ceiling exists.
findings.fix: State the non-cascade fuse explicitly in 04.04.03 D-02 (a default duration plus a ceiling, or platform-set by type), and reconcile D-07's 'a window they chose' with 04.04.04 D-05. Re-point 04.04.03 DT-06's bound at a live question rather than 04.04.04 Q-03, which is closed and cascade-scoped.

findings.claim: 04.04.02 permits the poster to signal 'still in consideration' to a shortlisted applicant; 04.04.01 D-06 forbids telling an applicant a state at all, naming that exact signal as a hope-raising rank leak.
findings.evidence: 04.04.02-shortlist-multi-reviewer-scoring.md:69 - "| Shortlisted applicant is never told | ... Default at Level 1: applicants are **not** auto-notified of shortlisting. **The poster may optionally signal \"still in consideration.\"** | Applicant sees no state change unless the poster explicitly signals." ; contradicted by 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md D-06 at :212 - "The applicant is told **a date, not a state** - \"You'll hear by 14 Aug\" | ... **Never \"you're a maybe\"** (raises hope, leaks a rank - the hazard 04.04.02 Q-02 identifies for shortlists), never silence" ; and 04.04.03:188, which extends the prohibition - "a \"pending offer\" hint **would leak a shortlist rank** (04.04.02 Q-02's hazard)". The stale-reference tail of the same defect sits at 04.05.04-applicant-pipeline-history.md:32, which lists a pipeline state for it and mis-cites the question as open - "| Shortlisted | If posters tell (**04.04.02 Q-02 - unresolved**) |" - while 04.04.02 Q-02 (:121) is resolved.

That is the leak D-06 and 04.04.03's Empty state are both written to prevent, and it lands on the applicant population domain D-07 protects from compounding rejection. An implementer following D-06 ships no such control, and 04.05.04's Shortlisted state is dead code.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a shortlisted applicant can be told anything other than a date, and whether the pipeline has a Shortlisted state.
findings.fix: Delete the optional 'still in consideration' signal from 04.04.02 (or scope it to a date restatement), and remove or re-label 04.05.04's Shortlisted entry state with a corrected citation.

findings.claim: The queue collapses a candidate to one card per identity and never addresses the two-candidacy case that its siblings require to render as two.
findings.evidence: 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:70 - "| **One candidate, one card** | **Regardless of how many times an identity submitted.** | D-10 |" ; D-10 at :216 - "**One candidate, one card**, regardless of submission count | ... The 50 submissions are an artefact, not evidence about the person, and **are not shown**." ; :129 - "| One identity submits 50 times | **One candidate, one card** (D-10) ... | Poster sees one card. **Nothing indicates the 50** |" ; contradicted by 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:95 - "| **Applicant applies to the same post in two roles** | **Two candidacies, not a supersede** ... (D-05, DT-05) | **Both live in the pipeline independently, each with its own disposition.** |" and :96 (same for self-plus-band) ; and by 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:155 - "| **One human applied to two slots on the same post** ... | **Two submissions, two obligations, answered independently.** Winning one slot does *not* disposition their candidacy on the other | Applicant: \"Won - keys. Still waiting - vocals.\" Both true simultaneously. |" ; and by opportunities-casting-cx.md:26 (CX-08) - "04.03.01 D-05 (one submission may carry two roles) makes the obligation's arithmetic **two dispositions owed per applicant**". 04.04.01 never mentions the case.
findings.failureScenario: A doubling keys player applies for both the keys slot and the vocals slot. The queue built from D-10 shows one card, so the poster makes one call and one disposition fires - and the second obligation stays open forever with no surface to discharge it, or is discharged by an act the poster never took. 04.05.01:155's promised applicant view ('Won - keys. Still waiting - vocals') is unreachable because the poster never had two cards to act on.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the queue renders one card per identity or one per candidacy.
findings.fix: Restate D-10 as one card per *candidacy* (keyed as F15 resolves it), with supersedes collapsing within a candidacy - which preserves D-10's anti-spam intent without colliding with 04.03.01 D-05 and 04.05.01 D-07.

findings.claim: 04.04.03 DT-04 characterises 04.01.03 D-05 as carrying a reconfirm-or-auto-withdraw rule, which the three decisions that own terms-change semantics explicitly reject.
findings.evidence: 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md DT-04 at :208 - "04.01.03 built an elaborate and well-reasoned apparatus - a publication gate (D-01), six mandatory facets (D-08), £0-is-not-a-fee (D-09), unrepresentable applicant fees (D-02), **versioned downward edits with reconfirm-or-auto-withdraw (D-05)**" ; contradicted by 04.01.03-compensation-spec-work-guardrails.md D-05 at :211 - "**Rejected auto-withdrawing on silence**: a musician who applied at £200 and never saw the notice should not lose their place over an unseen notice - the terms-set rule (04.01.01 D-09) makes silence keep them in" ; and by 04.01.01 D-09 at :270 - "there is **no auto-withdraw on silence, no silent grandfathering, and no suspend-until-reconfirm**" ; and by 04.01.04 D-06 at :103 - "there is no suspend-pending-reconfirm and no auto-withdraw-on-silence".
findings.failureScenario: An implementer reading 04.04.03's central Deep Think entry - the one that produced D-05, D-10 and most of its edge cases, and is therefore likely to be read closely - implements a reconfirm gate or an auto-withdraw on the applicant's silence after a downward compensation edit. That drops from the pool every applicant who did not see the notice, which is the specific harm 04.01.03 D-05 states it rejected, and it silently reduces the poster's close-out debt (04.05.01:159 - 'submitters who ignore the re-gate are still owed - silence is not consent and never reduces the debt').
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an unanswered terms-change notice withdraws, suspends or preserves the submission.
findings.fix: Correct the DT-04 clause to 'versioned downward edits with notify + [Stay]/[Withdraw], silence keeps the applicant in the pool (04.01.01 D-09)'.

findings.claim: 04.05.04 permits an applicant to withdraw while an offer is live and records it as a withdrawal; 04.03.01 D-12 scopes withdrawal to pre-offer states only and requires that act to be a decline - and the two paths have different reputation and offer-chain consequences.
findings.evidence: 04.05.04-applicant-pipeline-history.md:55 - "| Applicant withdraws while an offer is live | **Allowed** - withdraw is the applicant's own act, unlike self-close. **Entry moves to `withdrawn`**; the live offer's fuse is released back to the poster (04.05.03) | \"Withdrawn\" - and the offer is gone, deliberately irreversible |" ; D-06 at :98 - "| D-06 | Applicants **can withdraw** (unlike self-close), which **releases a live offer's fuse** back to the poster |" ; contradicted by 04.03.01-structured-submission.md D-12 at :202 - "**Withdrawal is scoped to pre-offer states only** | Withdraw, decline and break-a-commitment are three verbs with three costs and three owners (DT-07). **Once an offer is live the control hands to 04.04.03.**" ; and its edge case :100 - "| **Withdraw after an offer is live** | **Not a withdrawal - a decline** (D-12, DT-07). Control changes and hands off to 04.04.03. | The decline path, not the withdraw path. |" ; DT-07 at :155 records the conflation as the defect it fixed - "**Withdrawal and decline are different verbs and the state machine conflated them.**" The consequences differ materially: 04.05.01 D-09 (:243) excludes withdrawals "**from the denominator entirely**" while a decline is a poster-answered event that falls to #2 and carries a structured reason (04.04.03 D-11 at :255, CX-02 at :11).
findings.failureScenario: A dep is offered Saturday, then pulls out before the fuse burns. Under 04.05.04 D-06 the act is a withdrawal: the entry closes as `withdrawn`, the event leaves 04.05.02's denominator, and no structured decline reason is captured - so the poster loses the single most valuable repricing signal in the domain (04.04.03 DT-15) and the shortlist's fall-to-#2 trigger (CX-02) is not the one that fired. Under 04.03.01 D-12 the same act is a decline: it counts, it carries a reason, and #2 is offered. Two implementations produce different reputation arithmetic for the poster and a different next step for the shortlist, from the same user action.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a post-offer pull-out is a withdrawal or a decline, and therefore whether it enters the response-rate denominator and triggers the fall to #2.
findings.fix: Rewrite 04.05.04's row and D-06 to hand post-offer pull-outs to 04.04.03's decline path per 04.03.01 D-12, keeping withdrawal for pre-offer states; and add the resulting disposition value (see F27).

findings.claim: The disposition vocabulary is presented as complete and contains no value for a candidate declining a live offer, although declining is a first-class act with its own state and reason model in 04.04.03.
findings.evidence: 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:48 - "### Disposition values - **deliberately few**, and two columns that were one" ; the table at :54-62 enumerates seven values - `won`, `not selected`, `filled elsewhere`, `withdrawn by poster`, `withdrawn by applicant`, `expired`, `no-decision` - and scopes `expired` narrowly at :61: "| `expired` | **The applicant never answered an offer within its fuse** (04.04.03 D-02) | **System** |". A decline is neither. Meanwhile 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md makes it first-class: D-06 at :250 ("**The counter-offer is a first-class act**" with ":154 - countering under a cascade clock \"is a decline in practice\""), D-11 at :255 ("The decline carries an **optional, structured reason**"), the Declined state at :194 ("| Declined | Candidate declines | Falls to #2 (CX-02). Structured reason if given (D-11) |") and :142-143. 04.05.04's entry-state list at :37 mirrors the gap - "| Filled elsewhere / withdrawn / expired | Closed |" - with no declined state.
findings.failureScenario: Three plausible mappings, three different outcomes. Mapping the decline to `withdrawn by applicant` removes it from 04.05.02's denominator (04.05.01 D-09), so a poster whose fee is rejected by four of five candidates shows a perfect response rate. Mapping it to `filled elsewhere` credits the poster with answering someone who actually answered them, and requires a win that may never come. Adding an eighth value changes a vocabulary declared closed and every consumer that switches on it. The decline reason 04.04.03 D-11 collects has nowhere to live in any of the three.
findings.forcedInvention: Which disposition closes a declined candidacy, and whether it counts for, against, or outside the poster's response rate.
findings.fix: Add `declined by applicant` to 04.05.01's table with an explicit denominator rule (it is the applicant's act, so excluded like a withdrawal, but it carries D-11's reason), and add the matching entry state to 04.05.04.

findings.claim: The credit trigger's fire time is defined only relative to a scheduled end, which four of the nine handoff rows do not have - including both handoff targets that exist at launch.
findings.evidence: 04.05.03-won-opportunity-handoff.md D-16 at :245 - "**The handoff creates a dated credit trigger and a cast snapshot** | ... **Trigger fires at scheduled-end + 12h** - not at 1am load-out." ; :120 - "11. Sunday at **scheduled-end + 12 hours** ... the credit trigger fires." ; the handoff table at :50-60 routes four types to targets with no scheduled end: "| Session call | A contributor on a project | Join ... | 07 |", "| Brief / RFP | An engagement with scope + fee | Create | 05 |", "| Crew job | An engagement **and** a call sheet entry | Create (05) + Join (18) |", "| Camp invitation | A contributor on the camp project | Join | 07 |" - and 04.01.01 D-10 (:271) makes exactly those types deadline-shaped rather than wall-clock: "presence types carry venue-local wall-clock; **delivery types carry an absolute instant**". Those are the launch targets per this file's own Q-01 resolution at :254 - "**05 (engagements) and 07 (projects) are v1 targets and 17/18 are phase 2+**". The mechanism's importance is the file's own claim at DT-07 (:198): "it may be the most thesis-load-bearing thing in the domain".
findings.failureScenario: A won brief hands off to a 05 engagement with a delivery deadline and no scheduled end. Implementer A fires the credit prompt at deadline + 12h - before the work is necessarily delivered, so the confirmation asks 'did this happen?' about something that has not. Implementer B fires it on the downstream completion event, which is 05's and may never arrive. Implementer C does not create a trigger at all, and the credit becomes a reconstruction - the root cause the whole thesis is aimed at. The domain's central capture mechanism therefore has no defined clock for the only two targets available at launch.
findings.forcedInvention: The credit trigger's fire time for delivery-shaped types (session, brief, crew engagement, camp).
findings.fix: Give D-16 a per-shape clock: scheduled-end + 12h for presence types, and a delivery/acceptance event (or deadline + N) for delivery types, naming the event 05 and 07 must emit.
